MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
August 5, 2013

1.  OPENING CEREMONIES

a.  Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7:00 p.m., on Monday,
August 5, 2013, in the Council Chambers, at Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

b.  Flag Salute

Councilmember Savidan led the salute to the flag.

c.  Invocation

Councilmember Sanchez gave the invocation.

d.  Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Gazeley, Traina, Sanchez, Savidan, and Mayor Estrada. Also present were City Manager Rock,
Assistant City Manager Sugano, City Attorney Hogin, Public Works Director Damasse,
Community Services Director McPherron, Administrative Services Director Chavez, Parks and
Recreation Director Harding, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2.  PRESENTATIONS

Malisa Ellis-Watts introduced this year’s exchange students from Lomita’s Sister City, Takaishi,
Japan. John Vollmer, Lomita Sister City President, was also recognized by his colleagues and
students for his efforts and hard work with the Sister City Organization.

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Gazeley moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Sanchez seconded
the motion, which carried unanimously.

4. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock informed those in attendance about the upcoming start of the Crenshaw and
Lomita Boulevard Rehabilitation Project later this week, and stated that the estimated
completion date for the project is late September 2013.

City Manager Rock announced that the City of Lomita’s General Municipal Election will be held
on Tuesday, November 5, 2013, at which time three Councilmembers will be elected to four-
year terms. According to City Manager Rock, at the present time six Lomita residents have
qualified as candidates for the three Councilmember vacancies: Incumbent James Gazeley,
Incumbent Ben Traina, Mark Waronek, Dave Albert, Cindy Segawa, and James Thompson.
City Manager Rock added that those interested in running for one of the Councilmember

  Page 1
 vacancies can contact the City Clerk’s Office in order to schedule an appointment and pick-up
the required nomination papers.

5.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Joe McGrath, Lomita resident, stated that people are picking-up recyclables before scheduled
trash pick-ups, which in turn could jeopardize the City’s quotas for recyclables. Mr. McGrath
also mentioned that the cost of the computer tablet, as indicated in the demands, was
excessive.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, stated that he was concerned that small businesses in Lomita,
particularly real estate brokers, are paying higher business license fees than out-of-town
businesses, which in turn puts the small businesses in Lomita at a disadvantage. Mr. Kivett also
stated that he hopes the upcoming election will be clean and open, with no election signs being
removed by residents or opposing candidates.

Judy Daley, Representative of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, invited those in attendance to
the Chamber’s next Business Networking Mixer, which will take place at City Hall on Thursday,
August 22, 2013, from 8:00 a.m. to 9:30 a.m.

6. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Councilmember Traina requested a future agenda item to discuss the possibility of raising the
Transient Occupancy Tax (TOT), and to prepare a ballot measure regarding the tax for a future
election. Councilmembers Sanchez and Savidan concurred with Councilmember Traina’s
request to place the item on a future City Council meeting agenda.

Councilmember Sanchez reported that he attended a meeting of the League of California Cities.
Councilmember Sanchez also pointed out that the City of Lomita’s power usage is over
$136,000, according to a printout he received from the South Bay Cities Council of
Governments (SBCCOG). Subsequently, Councilmember Sanchez requested a future agenda
item to discuss the installation of solar power on all City facilities in order to save on energy
costs. Councilmembers Gazeley and Traina agreed with Councilmember Sanchez’s request to
place the item on a future Council meeting agenda.

Councilmember Savidan stated that staff needs to contact the Sheriff’s Department regarding
the recyclables issues and enforcement.

Councilmember Gazeley reported that he attended a meeting of the Los Angeles County West
Vector Control Board, and he urged citizens to take precautions against the West Nile Virus.
Councilmember Gazeley also stated that the City of Lomita was recognized by SBCCOG as the
first recipient of the platinum award for Energy Efficient Programs.  Furthermore,
Councilmember Gazeley recommended that the City look into replacing current street lights with
LED lights, which in turn would further reduce energy costs.

Councilmember Gazeley also reported that he attended a meeting of the Southern California
Economic Development Housing and SBCCOG. According to Councilmember Gazeley, one of
the discussions at SBCCOG meeting was about the Bay Delta Conservation Plan, as well as the
concerns associated with the aging water system in California and the possibility of

  Page 2
 earthquakes. Councilmember Gazeley stated that the City should be aware of this, and be
prepared by having a solution in case of an emergency.

Mayor Estrada invited those in attendance to the Lomita Sister City’s farewell party for the
exchange students, which will be held at the Tom Rico Center on Friday, August 9, 2013,
starting at 6 p.m. According to Mayor Estrada, the cost of the farewell party is $15 per person,
and she asked that attendees RSVP at 310-539-1399. Mayor Estrada also stated that the
Sheriff’s Department needs to be involved with the recyclables issues, as she has personally
witnessed people taking recyclables.

7. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Traina asked to pull Item 7.C. from the Consent Agenda. Councilmember
Savidan moved to approve the Consent Agenda, minus Item 7.C. Councilmember Traina
seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

Councilmember Traina asked for clarification regarding Voucher #510871, and why the cost of
the computer tablet was so high. City Manager Rock responded that the Microsoft Surface
(computer tablet) functions as a fully functioning computer, and not just a tablet.
Councilmember Sanchez moved to approve Item 7.C. Councilmember Savidan seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading.

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Regular City Council meeting held on
  July 15, 2013. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  d. Monthly Report for the Administrative Services Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  e. Monthly Report for the Community Development Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  f. Monthly Report for the Parks and Recreation Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  g. Monthly Report for the Public Works Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  h. Monthly Report regarding Economic Development Activities. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  i. June 2013 Treasurer’s Report. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  j. Adoption of a Resolution in support of the Los Angeles County Division of the League of
  California Cities’ resolution requesting that the the Governor and Legislature work with
  local governments to assist in funding stormwater projects. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  Page 3
   PUBLIC HEARING

8.  CONGESTION MANAGEMENT PLAN (CMP)

  Councilmember Sanchez moved to table this item to the next agenda. Councilmember
  Gazeley seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

  SCHEDULED MATTERS

9.  Discussion/Consideration of an award of a Public Works Contract to Stephen Doreck
  Equipment Rentals, Inc. in the amount of $1,699,398 (with a 20% contingency for a
  total project budget of $2,039,278) for the Eshelman Avenue Water Main Replacement
  and Street Resurfacing Project from Pacific Coast Highway to Lomita Boulevard.

  Public Works Director Damasse provided a PowerPoint presentation (Attachment A).
  Director Damasse provided an overview of the timeline for the project and stated that limits
  of the project are from Pacific Coast Highway to Lomita Boulevard, with the scope of work
  consisting of the construction of a new 8-inch water main, the abandoning of the existing 6-
  inch water main, and construction of fire hydrants, new service laterals, and water meters.
  In addition, Director Damasse stated that project will include pavement resurfacing, which
  will include grinding 2-3 inches of the existing asphalt, the placement of rubberized chip
  seal, resurfacing with asphalt rubber hot mix, and striping. Director Damasse recommended
  that City Council award construction of the project to the Stephen Doreck Equipment
  Rentals, Inc., as well as approval of a 20% contingency to cover any utility and other
  unforeseen issues associated with the project.
  Discussion followed on whether the 20% contingency was too high. Councilmember
  Sanchez asked if staff had looked into the possibility of replacing the light poles with more
  aesthetically pleasing ones, as was previously requested by Councilmember Traina.
  George Kivett, Lomita resident, expressed concern regarding water pressure if the size of
  the water lines are increased from six to eight inches. Mr. Kivett also asked staff to be
  cautious in order to minimize the impact on residents and commercial businesses.
  Councilmember Traina moved to approve the award as recommended by staff for items #9
  and #10. Councilmember Gazeley seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.
10. Discussion/Consideration of approving a Professional Services Agreement with
  AndersonPenna Partners Inc. for Construction Management Services for the
  Eshelman Avenue Water Main Replacement and Street Resurfacing Project in the
  amount of $146,638 (with a 15% contingency for a total project budget of $168,633).

  This item was discussed in conjunction with Item 9.
11. Distribution of Lomita Golf Tournament proceeds.
  Presented by Parks and Recreation Director Harding
  Parks and Recreation Director Harding stated that $19,090 was raised as a result of the 7th
  Annual Mayor’s Cup and Gold Classic. According to Director Harding, after taking into

  Page 4
   account all expenses associated with the tournament, the total net proceeds are $9,238.85.
  Director Harding recommended that City Council authorizes funding for the Teen Program ($
  5,000), the Youth Golf Program ($1,238.85), and the Youth Basketball Program ($3,000)
  with the proceeds from the tournament.
  Councilmember Gazeley thanked Mayor Estrada and Charles Felix for all their time and
  efforts associated with putting on the tournament.
  Councilmember Traina moved to approve the use of the proceeds from the tournament as
  recommended by staff. Councilmember Sanchez seconded the motion, which carried
  unanimously.
ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 8:00 p.m., in memory of Rita Miller.

Respectfully Submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
